description: Over 4-5 January 2020, days after the killing of Qasem Soleimani, CBP held more than 60 American citizens and green card holders of Iranian heritage at Blaine, Washington, for up to 11-12 hours, questioning them about family, politics and allegiance to Iran.
time_note: Up to 12 hours in a single day.
energy_note: Questioned on loyalty as a citizen of the country doing the questioning.

description: A January 2020 Senate letter cited more than 60 held and up to 200 affected. A November 2021 congressional letter revised this to more than 80 held on 5 January 2020 with nearly 300 affected, some held over 10 hours and others turned away for lack of space.

Documents released under litigation - 237 pages ordered released by Chief Judge Ricardo Martinez - included a 7 January email stating the Seattle Field Office advised ports to refer all encounters with individuals 'from areas of national concern' to secondary. Proposed guidance required secondary inspection for individuals born after 1961 and before 2001 who met criteria including being 'Iranian and Lebanese nationals'.
energy_note: Nationality plus birth year, in writing.
notes: This and the NSIRA finding (SEC-001) are the two hardest documentary anchors in the dataset: both show selection by demographic category.

description: CBP stated it did not detain anyone because of country of origin, which first-hand accounts and the released records contradict. Lawmakers noted that traffic and staffing explanations did not account for why those affected were overwhelmingly of Iranian heritage or why pre-cleared travellers were delayed.
energy_note: Officially told the thing that happened to you did not happen.

description: Those held included NEXUS trusted-traveller holders, who had already passed background vetting, and were asked about political views, allegiances and ties to the Iranian military.
The lasting cost is behavioural: people stop crossing, stop travelling, stop visiting relatives in Canada. A single weekend reshapes years of movement.

aspect: EXAMPLE - turned away for lack of space
description: Some travellers were not merely delayed but turned away because the secondary inspection area had no room left.
energy_note: Refused entry to your own country because the queue was full.

description: An immigration attorney present reported a CBP officer describing it as 'extreme vetting', saying every Iranian was being sent to the port director for a final decision.
Those held included US citizens, permanent residents and people of all ages including the elderly and children.
